claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a heterogeneous microstructure containing coarse grains.
The starting alloy contains unevenly distributed brittle intermetallic phases.
High-pressure/high-temperature treatment in a hexahedron-anvil apparatus will refine the alloy's grain structure.
The treatment will reduce intermetallic cluster size.
The treatment will produce a more uniform phase distribution.
Combined high pressure and high temperature accelerate diffusion in the alloy.
Combined high pressure and high temperature induce dynamic recrystallization in the alloy.
Accelerated diffusion and dynamic recrystallization cause grain refinement and redistribution of brittle phases.
Microstructural homogenization caused by the treatment increases yield strength.
Reduced connectivity of brittle phases improves ductility.
Treated samples will have greater yield strength than samples not receiving the high-pressure/high-temperature intervention.
Treated samples will have greater ductility than samples not receiving the high-pressure/high-temperature intervention.
The anticipated increases in yield strength and ductility are each greater than 10%.
The predicted response is limited to eutectic high-entropy alloys whose microstructural heterogeneities can be modified by dynamic recrystallization.
Alloys with compositions or initial phase distributions not amenable to dynamic-recrystallization-driven modification may not exhibit the predicted improvements.

contradictions.description: The comparator is described variously as 'untreated samples,' samples receiving standard post-solidification treatments, and a control group that receives no high-pressure/high-temperature treatment. These may represent different thermal or processing histories and therefore do not define one unambiguous baseline.
